.. or reboot the phone (these iptable rules are not persistent)



CAUTION

Do NOT edit one of the config files for dnsmasq while dnsmasq is running! This will most likely destroy the file!

Because of this "feature", the script customize.sh creates an initial backup copy (*.bak) of each of the text files in the sub directories in /data/local/tmp/sysroot/dnsmasq.



Using the dnsmasq as PXE server

The Magisk module also includes all the necessary files to use the dnsmasq server as a PXE server for booting Linux or other operating systems over the network.

Note that the DHCP server from dnsmasq must be enabled to use dnsmasq as PXE server (or configure the IP address of the phone with the running dnsmasq as next server in the DHCP server for the network)
If a DHCP server is already running on the network, configure dnsmasq to handle only those computers for which a static IP address has been configured in the dnsmasq configuration files.

The files for the PXE functionality are in the directory /data/local/tmp/sysroot/dnsmasq/tftp.

If the PXE server is to be used exclusively for booting Linux live rescue images via the PXE server, no additional configuration is required -- in this case, the default configuration for the PXE server is sufficient.


The default PXE config file in the Magisk Module, /data/local/tmp/sysroot/dnsmasq/tftp/pxelinux.cfg/default, already contains sample boot entries for these Linux rescue CDs:


Linux distribution
 Homepage
 Comment
grml https://grml.org/
SystemRescue https://www.system-rescue.org/
CloneZilla https://clonezilla.org/
Puppy https://wikka.puppylinux.com/HomePage


The default PXE boot menue in this Magisk module looks like this:




To boot a PC or virtual machine from one of these live images on your phone via the PXE server, download the ISO images for the distribution and copy the contents of the ISO image to the approbiate directory on your phone:

Linux distribution
 target directory on the phone for the contents of the ISO image
 Comment
grml /data/local/tmp/sysroot/dnsmasq/tftp/grml
systemrescue /data/local/tmp/sysroot/dnsmasq/tftp/systemrescue
clonezilla /data/local/tmp/sysroot/dnsmasq/tftp/clonezilla
puppy /data/local/tmp/sysroot/dnsmasq/tftp/puppy


The configuration for the images systemrescue and grml in the default PXE config file in the Magisk module use http to download the image files with the filesystem.
Therefore, it's necessary to start the http daemon darkhttpd on the phone before booting a PC from one of these images:

/data/local/tmp/darkhttpd /data/local/tmp/sysroot/dnsmasq/tftp/


One small Linux Live CD is already included in the Magisk Module:

SliTaz

ASUS_I006D:/ $ ls -lh /data/local/tmp/sysroot/dnsmasq/tftp/slitaz/
total 54K
-rw-rw-rw- 1 shell shell 3.6M 2026-02-16 09:31 bzImage64
-rw-rw-rw- 1 shell shell  50M 2026-04-05 03:32 rootfs.gz
ASUS_I006D:/ $


SliTax is a lightweight Linux distribution that can be used for simple maintenance tasks (see https://www.slitaz.org for more details)

Note: 

The user for SliTax is "root" with the password "root"; the non-root user in SliTax is "tux" without a password.

There is an online builder for SliTax that allows you to create your own SliTax ISO image: https://pizza.slitaz.org/ 


To add another rescue CD, simply copy the files from that CD into a new sub directory in /data/local/tmp/sysroot/dnsmasq/tftp and add a new entry for the rescue CD in the PXE config file /data/local/tmp/sysroot/dnsmasq/tftp/pxelinux.cfg/default.



Trouble Shooting



In some Android distributions the file /system/bin/dnsmasq is not readable by the user shell (for example in /e/):

ASUS_I006D:/ $ id
 uid=2000(shell) gid=2000(shell) groups=2000(shell),1004(input),1007(log),1011(adb),1015(sdcard_rw),1028(sdcard_r),1078(ext_data_rw),1079(ext_obb_rw),3001(net_bt_admin),3002(net_bt),3003(inet),3006(net_bw_stats),3009(readproc),3011(uhid),3012(readtracefs) context=u:r:shell:s0
 ASUS_I006D:/ $

ASUS_I006D:/ $ ls /system/bin/dnsmasq
 ls: /system/bin/dnsmasq: Permission denied
 1|ASUS_I006D:/ $


But the user root can read and execute the dnsmasq binary:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ su -c ls /system/bin/dnsmasq
/system/bin/dnsmasq
ASUS_I006D:/ $

ASUS_I006D:/ $ su -c /system/bin/dnsmasq --version
Dnsmasq version 2.92rc3  Copyright (c) 2000-2025 Simon Kelley
Compile time options: IPv6 GNU-getopt no-DBus no-UBus no-i18n no-IDN DHCP DHCPv6 Lua TFTP no-conntrack ipset no-nftset auth no-DNSSEC loop-detect inotify dumpfile

This software comes with ABSOLUTELY NO WARRANTY.
Dnsmasq is free software, and you are welcome to redistribute it
under the terms of the GNU General Public License, version 2 or 3.
ASUS_I006D:/ $ 


That's because there is a dedicated SELinux context for dnsmasq in the OS:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ su -c ls -Z /system/bin/dnsmasq
u:object_r:dnsmasq_exec:s0 /system/bin/dnsmasq
ASUS_I006D:/ $


To get around this, use the scripts from the Magisk Module to start/stop dnsmasq (the scripts use "su -c" to execute dnsmasq binary)

Note:

To configure the missing SELinux rules this command can be use:

 magiskpolicy --live "allow shell dnsmasq_exec file { getattr execute read open execute_no_trans map }"

But be aware, that root access is required to use dnsmasq.



If the start of the dnsmasq in the script service.sh fails, the script creates the log file

/data/local/tmp/dnsmasq.log

example:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ cat /data/local/tmp/dnsmasq.log
Error starting dnsmasq:

dnsmasq: failed to create listening socket for 127.0.0.1: Address already in use
ASUS_I006D:/ $



If the DHCP server from dnsmasq does not start, check that there is at least one entry for dhcp-range in the dnsmasq config file.


To debug errors, stop the dnsmasq 

stop_dnsmasq

and start dnsmasq manually in the foreground:

su -c dnsmasq -d -q --log-queries --log-dhcp  

Example
ASUS_I006D:/ $ stop_dnsmasq
 Stopping the dnsmasq ...
 ASUS_I006D:/ $
ASUS_I006D:/ $ su -c dnsmasq -d -q --log-queries --log-dhcp  
dnsmasq: started, version 2.92rc3 cachesize 150
 dnsmasq: compile time options: IPv6 GNU-getopt no-DBus no-UBus no-i18n no-IDN DHCP DHCPv6 Lua TFTP no-conntrack ipset no-nftset auth no-DNSSEC loop-detect inotify dumpfile
 dnsmasq-tftp: TFTP root is /data/local/tmp/sysroot/dnsmasq/tftp 
dnsmasq: reading /data/local/tmp/sysroot/dnsmasq/etc/resolv.conf
 dnsmasq: using nameserver 1.1.1.1#53
 dnsmasq: using nameserver 8.8.8.8#53
 dnsmasq: read /data/local/tmp/sysroot/dnsmasq/etc/hosts - 5 names


----


If you encounter errors due to a failed connection, please check the configuration of the active firewall on the phone and on the PC.


Please note that the dnsmasq binary for Android does not work if no IP address is configured for the wlan0 interface. Therefore, if you are using dnsmasq as the sole DHCP server on a network, you must configure a static IP address for the wlan0 interface..


see also the general notes in the section Implementation details for all Magisk Modules   


 
Sourcecode

The source code for dnsmasq is available in this GitHub repository:

https://github.com/imp/dnsmasq


The dnsmasq binary for Android running on arm64 CPUs is also available here:

http://bnsmb.de/files/public/Android/binaries_for_arm64/dnsmasq

and in the GitHub repository with binaries for Android:

https://github.com/bnsmb/binaries-for-Android

Documentation for the Magisk Module with gcc

The Magisk Module with gcc contains a toolchain with the gcc 16.x and the sysroot from the Android NDK r30 compiled for arm64 CPUs

Also included are the binaries make, pkg-config, and pkgconf.


The Magisk Module is also available in this GitHub repository:

https://github.com/bnsmb/magisk-modules/


The gcc toolchain was copied from this GitHub repository:

https://github.com/AmanoTeam/android-gcc-cross


Note

The GitHub repository also contains gcc binaries for other CPUs. The Magisk Module only contains the files for arm64 CPUs.


The version of the gcc and g++ in the Magisk Module is:

ASUS_I006D:/data/local/tmp # gcc --version
aarch64-unknown-linux-android-gcc (GCC) 16.2.1 20261006
Copyright (C) 2026 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
This is free software; see the source for copying conditions.  There is NO
warranty; not even for MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

ASUS_I006D:/data/local/tmp #

ASUS_I006D:/system/bin # g++ --version
aarch64-unknown-linux-android-g++ (GCC) 16.2.1 20261006
Copyright (C) 2026 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
This is free software; see the source for copying conditions.  There is NO
warranty; not even for MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

ASUS_I006D:/system/bin #


The gcc toolchain is installed in the directory

/system/lib/android-gcc-cross/

Symbolic links to the executables in the gcc toolchain are in the directory

/system/bin/gcc-toolchain


Symbolic links for cc, c++, gcc and g++ are installed in the directory /system/bin.

cc, c++, gcc, and g++ are wrapper scripts for the real compiler.

The wrapper scripts use the value of the environment variable API to select the compiler to use. The default value for the environment variable API in the scripts is 31.
(API 31 is Android 12 -- see https://source.android.com/docs/setup/reference/build-numbers)

Note: The original wrapper scripts from the gcc toolchain use an API version hardcoded in the scripts.


The include and lib directories from the sysroot in the Android NDK is in the directory

/system/lib/android-gcc-cross

To compile a file with gcc or g++ using CMake, use one of the CMake toolchain files from the /system/lib/android-gcc-cross/usr/local/share/android-gcc-cross/cmake directory.

Example:

API=31 cmake \
  -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=/system/lib/android-gcc-cross/usr/local/share/android-gcc-cross/cmake/aarch64-unknown-linux-android${API}.cmake \
  -G Ninja ..


Note:

Compiling C/C++ files with CMake and gcc was tested with the cmake from this Magisk Module: http://bnsmb.de/files/public/Android/MagiskModules/cmake_4.4.2-v1.1.0.zip


The script

/system/bin/init_gcc_env

can be used to init the environment for the gcc toolchain to use the other binaries from the gcc toolchain without fully qualified name.

Currently the script only extends the PATH variable and the prompt. To use it execute the command

source /system/bin/init_gcc_env

Note that this is not necessary to use the gcc or g++.


Internals


To create the Magisk Module, the gcc toolchain was installed in /system using the installation script for Termux from the repository with the gcc toolchain with a few modifications.

The shell script used to download the script from the repository, make these modifications, and install the gcc using the modified script  -- install_gcc.sh -- is in the directory ./source in the Magisk module.


To make /system writable, an overlay mount for /system was used. The overlay mount was created with the script

create_overlay_mount.sh


The script create_overlay_mount.sh is also available in the GitHub repository with scripts for Android:

https://github.com/bnsmb/scripts-for-Android/blob/main/scripts/create_overlay_mount.sh


see the Documentation_for_the_script_create_overlay_mount.sh.html for the documentation for the script

Please note that the tar archive with the gcc toolchain in the repository is compressed with xz. Therefore, a xz binary is required to unpack that file.
xz ist not installed by default in Android; an xz binary for arm64 CPUs can be downloaded here:  http://bnsmb.de/files/public/Android/binaries_for_arm64/xz
The xz binary is also in the GitHub repository with binaries for Android on arm64 CPUs.


The script for installing the GCC toolchain is also available for download separately here:

install_gcc.sh

The script is also available in the GitHup repository with scripts for Android:

https://github.com/bnsmb/scripts-for-Android
 
Note

The definition for the target directory for the installation is at the begin of the script install_gcc.sh:

[xtrnaw7@t15g /data/develop/android/ModuleSrc/gcc16]$ egrep "^GCC_INSTALL_DIR=|^TOOLCHAIN_LINK_DIRECTORY=" install_gcc.sh
GCC_INSTALL_DIR="/system/lib/android-gcc-cross"
TOOLCHAIN_LINK_DIRECTORY="/system//bin/gcc-toolchain/"
[xtrnaw7@t15g /data/develop/android/ModuleSrc/gcc16]$




Trouble Shooting

The error message

shell-init: error retrieving current directory: getcwd: cannot access parent directories: Math result not representable

is caused by a bug in the bash binary on most Android versions.  In most cases, this message can be ignored (see here for details)

The scripts from the gcc toolchain must be executed by bash -- the default shell in Android, /system/bin/sh, does not support all required features used in these scripts.

To avoid the error message, install the bash binary from this Magisk Module:

bash_5.2.37-v1.2.0.zip

That bash binary is also available for download here:

bash-5.2.37

and in the GitHub repository with binaries for Android : https://github.com/bnsmb/binaries-for-Android

The source code for gdb is available here: https://sourceware.org/gdb/download/

The source code for the GNU BinUtils is available for download here: https://sourceware.org/pub/binutils/releases/


The patches from Termux for gdb and the GNU Binutils are applied.


In version 18.1 of gdb the code for using colors changed and does not work anymore in adb sessions (at least in my tests ...)

Therefore, color support is disabled by default in the gdb binaries in this Magisk module. To enable color support, set the COLOR environment variable to a non-empty value before starting gdb, for example:

COLOR=1 ./gdb -tui ...

Documentation for the Magisk Module with httpd


URL: https://xdaforums.com/t/module-a-magisk-module-with-an-http-server.4797095/


Documentation for the Magisk Module with httpd

This Magisk module with httpd contains darkhttpd 1.17, a simple httpd, and stunnel 5.77 to add https support.

All binaries in the Magisk module are compiled for Android on arm64 CPUs and require only standard libraries from the Android OS.


Use the command

darkhttpd <httpd_home_dir>

to start the httpd.

With the default config the webserver darkhttpd started as non-root users listens on the port 8080 for http requests only.


To access the webserver on the phone via http use this URL:

http://<ip_of_your_phone>:8080/



To add support for https to darkhttpd, the binary stunnel can be used.

The Magisk module contains a sample config file for stunnel to add https support for darkhttpd:

/system/etc/stunnel_for_darkhttpd


The file looks like this:

cat /system/etc/stunnel_for_darkhttpd
ASUS_I006D:/ $ cat /system/etc/stunnel_for_darkhttpd
; stunnel.conf - HTTPS wrapper for  darkhttpd (stunnel is listening on the port 8443 and forwards the requests to port 8080)
;
; Based on : https://www.stunnel.org/static/stunnel.html

; global settings
;
; create the directories if they do not yet exist (without the directories stunnel does not run):
;
; mkdir -p data/local/tmp/sysroot/var/run /data/local/tmp/sysroot/var/log
;
pid = /data/local/tmp/sysroot/var/run/stunnel.pid
debug = 7
output = /data/local/tmp/sysroot/var/log/stunnel.log
syslog = no

; run stunnel in the foreground; remove the line to start stunnel in the background
foreground = yes

; create the directories and the certificate if it does not yet exist
;
; mkdir -p /data/local/tmp/sysroot/etc/ssl/certs /data/local/tmp/sysroot/etc/ssl/private
;
; use the command
;
; openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout /data/local/tmp/sysroot/etc/ssl/private/server.key -out /data/local/tmp/sysroot/etc/ssl/certs/server.crt
;
; to create a self-signed certificate
;
cert = /data/local/tmp/sysroot/etc/ssl/certs/server.crt
key = /data/local/tmp/sysroot/etc/ssl/private/server.key

; optional:
;
sslVersion = TLSv1.2
options = NO_SSLv2
options = NO_SSLv3
options = SINGLE_DH_USE
options = SINGLE_ECDH_USE
ciphers = HIGH:!aNULL:!eNULL:!EXPORT:!DES:!RC4:!MD5:!PSK:!SRP

; HTTPS service for darkhttpd
[https]
accept = 8443
connect = 127.0.0.1:8080
TIMEOUTclose = 0
; Optional: Forward secrecy
curve = secp384r1

ASUS_I006D:/ $



To add SSL support for darkhttpd using that config file, create the necessary directories and files for stunnel:

# create the directories
#
mkdir -p /data/local/tmp/sysroot/var/run /data/local/tmp/sysroot/var/log
mkdir -p /data/local/tmp/sysroot/etc/ssl/certs /data/local/tmp/sysroot/etc/ssl/private

# create the self-signed certificate (or copy an already existing certificate)
#
openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout /data/local/tmp/sysroot/etc/ssl/private/server.key -out /data/local/tmp/sysroot/etc/ssl/certs/server.crt


and start stunnel after starting darkhttpd using this command:


stunnel /system/etc//stunnel_for_darkhttpd


To access the webserver on the phone via https use this URL:

https://<ip_of_your_phone>:8443/



Notes


The hardcoded default config file for stunnel is : /data/local/tmp/sysroot/etc/stunnel/stunnel.conf   


To automatically start darkhttpd after every reboot of the phone, create the file

/data/adb/modules/httpd/service.sh

with the commands to start darkhttpd and, optional, stunnel.

Example:

ASUS_I006D:/ # cat /data/adb/modules/httpd/service.sh
/system/bin/darkhttpd --port 8080 /sdcard  2>/dev/null >/dev/null &

/system/bin/stunnel /system/etc/stunnel_for_darkhttpd 2>/dev/null >/dev/null &
ASUS_I006D:/


Note that darkhttpd started from the service.sh script runs as user root and uses the port 80. To use another port, add the parameter "--port number" to the command to start darkhttpd.


stunnel can also be used to add SSL support for other daemons that do not support SSL.

added sample URLs for accessing the webserver via http or https

The Magisk Module network_tools contains various network related CLI tools for Android:

Tool

bmon
 bmon is a monitoring and debugging tool to capture networking related statistics and prepare them visually in a human friendly way https://github.com/tgraf/bmon
 bmon needs root access
 1.0.0
ngrep
 ngrep is a grep for network packets https://github.com/jpr5/ngrep ngrep needs root access
 1.0.0
dig, mdig, host, nsloookup, nsupdate
 dig is the Linux tool for hostname resolution via DNS server

mdig, host, nslookup, and nsupdate can also be used for hostname resolution.
 https://gitlab.isc.org/ The binaries dig, mdig, host, nslookup, and nsupdate are from bind 9.11


"mdig is a multiple/pipelined query version of dig: instead of waiting for a response after sending each query, it begins by sending all queries.
Responses are displayed in the order in which they are received, not in the order the corresponding queries were sent."

The binaries from bind use the file /etc/resolv.conf to get the nameserver to use. The file resolv.conf in the Magisk Module is:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ cat /system/etc/resolv.conf                                                                                               
nameserver 8.8.8.8
nameserver 1.1.1.1

ASUS_I006D:/ $

To use dig on phones without the file resolv.conf use the dig parameter for the nameserver to use - for example to ask the nameserver 192.168.1.1:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ dig www.heise.de @192.168.1.1 +short
193.99.144.85
ASUS_I006D:/ $

To change the default nameserver, edit the file /data/adb/modules/network_tools/system/etc/resolv.conf. 

(Download link for the source: https://gitlab.isc.org/isc-projects/bind9/-/branches?state=all&sort=updated_desc&search=9.11)

Documentation for the Magisk Module with nrpe

The Magisk Module with nrpe contains the binaries for the Nagios Remote Plugin Executor compiled for arm64 CPUs that can be used to monitor the Android OS with Nagios or a Nagios derivate such as, for example, Icinga.


The module contains the binaries nrpe and check_nrpe:

ASUS_I006D:/ # nrpe --version
NRPE - Nagios Remote Plugin Executor
Version: 4.1.3

3|ASUS_I006D:/ # check_nrpe --version                                                                                                                          


ASUS_I006D:/ # check_nrpe --version                                                                                                                          
NRPE Plugin for Nagios
Version: 4.1.3

3|ASUS_I006D:/ #


The module also includes a sample config file: /etc/nrpe.cfg and a test check script: /system/usr/nagios/libexec/check_test.sh:

ASUS_I006D:/ # grep "^command\[" /etc/nrpe.cfg
command[check_test]=/system/usr/nagios/libexec/check_test.sh
ASUS_I006D:/ #


To test the functionality of the nrpe binary open an adb session and start the nrpe daemon:

# start nrpe
#
ASUS_I006D:/ $ nrpe -n -c /etc/nrpe.cfg -d                                                                                                                                                                                       
ASUS_I006D:/ $


# check that the nrpe daemon is running
#
ASUS_I006D:/ $ ps -ef | grep -v grep | grep nrpe                                                                                                                                                                                 
shell        10509     1 0 13:37:18 ?     00:00:00 nrpe -n -c /etc/nrpe.cfg -d
ASUS_I006D:/ $


To test the nrpe daemon execute this command after starting the nrpe daemon:

2|ASUS_I006D:/ $ check_nrpe -H localhost -n  -c check_test 
OK, no error or warning file found
ASUS_I006D:/ $


# simulate a warning issue for the check check_test
#
ASUS_I006D:/ # touch /data/local/tmp/signal_warning
ASUS_I006D:/ #

ASUS_I006D:/ $ check_nrpe -H localhost -n  -c check_test 
WARNING: Warning file found
1|ASUS_I006D:/ $

# simulate an error issue for the check check_test
#
1|ASUS_I006D:/ # touch /data/local/tmp/signal_error
ASUS_I006D:/ #

ASUS_I006D:/ $ check_nrpe -H localhost -n  -c check_test
ERROR: Error file found
2|ASUS_I006D:/ $


Some other NRPE plugins compiled for Android are in the directory

/system/usr/nagios/libexec


ls -l /system/usr/nagios/libexec


ASUS_I006D:/ $ date
Sat Aug 29 13:41:49 CEST 2026
ASUS_I006D:/ $

ASUS_I006D:/ $ ls -l /system/usr/nagios/libexec

The module also contains a script to start or stop the nrpe daemon :

/system/bin/start_stop_nrpe.sh

The script start_stop_nrpe.sh can be used either in a shell or as action.sh script for the Magisk module.


The syntax for the script start_stop_nrpe.sh when executed in a shell is:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ start_stop_nrpe.sh

  start_stop_nrpe.sh [help] [start] [restart] [stop] [status] [enable] [disable] [viewlog] [var=value]
 
 Parameter:
 
   help       - print the usage help and exit_program
   start      - start the nrpe daemon
   restart    - restart the nrpe daemon
   stop       - stop the nrpe daemon
   status     - print the status of the nrpe daemon
   enable     - enable the automatic start of the nrpe daemon
   disable    - disable the automatic start of the nrpe daemon
   viewlog    - view the log file of the nrpe daemon
   clear      - clear the log file
   var=value  - set the variable "var" to the value "value"
                this parameter can be used multiple times

ASUS_I006D:/ $


The script start_stop_nrpe.sh searches the config file for nrpe in this order:

/data/local/tmp/sysroot/etc/nrpe.cfg
/data/local/tmp/nrpe.cfg
/system/etc/nrpe.cfg

To use a user defined config file, set the environment variable NRPE_CONFIG_FILE before executing start_stop_nrpe.sh .



When started via action.sh script, the script start_stop_nrpe.sh prints a menu in which the user can select a menu entry with the VolumeUp key and the VolumeDown key and execute the menu entry with the Power key

Example:







When no key is pressed in the first 10 seconds, the start_stop_nrpe.sh script automatically starts the nrpe daemon if it's not running or stops the nrpe daemon if it is already running:




Press either the VolumeUp key or the VolumeDown key to stop the timeout and select another menu entry:




Now you can execute any of the menu entries; to end the menu select the menu entry "Quit" .




The script also updates the module description in the Magisk module list, example:







To enable the automatic start of the nrpe daemon after a reboot either use the menu entry in the menu visible after pressing the Action button or execute the command

start_stop_nrpe.sh enable


This command must only run once. Execute the command

start_stop_nrpe.sh disable

to disable the automatic start of the nrpe daemon after a reboot.


Notes

The nrpe daemon is running as user shell; therefor the script start_stop_nrpe.sh can be executed by the user shell (that is the default user in adb shells).

To run the nrpe daemon as another user, modify these settings in the nrpe config file:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ grep shell /system/etc/nrpe.cfg
 nrpe_user=shell
 nrpe_group=shell
 ASUS_I006D:/ $

Be aware that when running the nrpe daemon with another user, the script start_stop_nrpe.sh must be executed by that user or the user root.

When the script start_stop_nrpe.sh is started via the action.sh script, the script is always executed by the user root.


The logfile used by the nrpe daemon is

ASUS_I006D:/ $ grep ^log_file /system/etc/nrpe.cfg                                                                                                     
log_file=/data/local/tmp/nrpe.log
ASUS_I006D:/ $


The semaphore file to enable the automatic start of the nrpe daemon after a reboot is

/data/local/tmp/START_NRPE


The nrpe daemon is compiled with SSL support.


The script start_stop_nrpe.sh starts the nrpe daemon without SSL support. To start the SSL daemon with SSL support, modify the entries for SSL in the nrpe config file nrpe.cfg and comment the line

NRPE_ADD_PARAMETER="${NRPE_ADD_PARAMETER:=-n}"

in the script start_stop_nrpe.sh. Then restart the nrpe daemon.


The documentation for the nrpe daemon is in the Magisk module in the directory /system/usr/nagios/doc:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ ls -l /system/usr/nagios/doc
total 360
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 114822 2026-08-25 08:56 NRPE.odt
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 223391 2026-08-25 08:56 NRPE.pdf
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root  11692 2026-08-25 08:56 README.SSL.md
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root   9688 2026-08-25 08:56 README.md

The script start_stop_nrpe.sh supports these environment variables:

Variable
 Description
 Default value
 Comment
READ_TIMEOUT timeout in seconds
 10
 set the variable to "none" to disable the timeout
NRPE_BINARY
 fully qualified name of the nrpe binary
 /system/bin/nrpe
NRPE_ADD_PARAMETER
 additional parameter for starting nrpe
 -n
 -n = do not use SSL
use "none" to disable the additional parameter


To use the envrionment variables use either this format for the command

var=value start_stop_nrpe.sh [parameter_for_the_script]

or this format:

start_stop_nrpe.sh var=value [parameter_for_the_script]


Add the variables to the file /data/adb/modules/nrpe/service.sh to change the settings for the automatic start of the nrpe daemon.


The home page for the official Nagios Plugins is here:

https://www.nagios.org/downloads/nagios-plugins/


Trouble Shooting

The reason for an error message like this

CHECK_NRPE: Receive header underflow - only -1 bytes received (4 expected).

or

CHECK_NRPE: Error - Could not connect to 127.0.0.1: Connection reset by peer


is most probably that the nrpe daemon is running with SSL support and check_nrpe was executed without SSL support (or vice versa)

To fix the error, use the parameter "-n" (= disable SSL support) for nrpe and check_nrpe or none of them.

Documentation for the Magisk Module with OpenSSH


URL: https://xdaforums.com/t/module-openssh-for-android.4696499/post-89966936


Notes:

This documentation is only valid for the Magisk Module with OpenSSH 9.9p2 or newer.

See the post https://xdaforums.com/t/module-openssh-for-android.4696499/ for the documentation of the Magisk Modules with OpenSSH 9.9p1.  

I have also created a tar archive with the OpenSSH binaries that can be used on phones without Magisk -- see How to connect to Android via ssh as user shell without root access  
 


Documentation for the Magisk Module with OpenSSH

The Magisk Module openssh contains the server and client binaries from OpenSSH for Android running on a arm64 CPU.


The latest working version of the Magisk Module with OpenSSH is OpenSSH 10.3p1 using OpenSSL 3.5.7:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ /system/bin/sshd -V
OpenSSH_10.3p1, OpenSSL 3.5.7 9 Jun 2026
ASUS_I006D:/ $


There is also a Magisk Module with OpenSSH 10.0p2 using OpenSSL 3.5.7:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ /system/bin/sshd -V
OpenSSH_10.0p2, OpenSSL 3.5.7 9 Jun 2026
ASUS_I006D:/ $


The OpenSSH binaries are compiled with SELinux support.


All executables are dynamically linked but only for the standard Android libraries, e.g.:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ ldd /system/bin/sshd
    linux-vdso.so.1 => [vdso] (0x70b7d31000)
    libdl.so => /apex/com.android.runtime/lib64/bionic/libdl.so (0x70b61f4000)
    libc.so => /apex/com.android.runtime/lib64/bionic/libc.so (0x70b6086000)
ASUS_I006D:/ $

ASUS_I006D:/ $ ldd /system/bin/ssh
    linux-vdso.so.1 => [vdso] (0x70eb265000)
    libdl.so => /apex/com.android.runtime/lib64/bionic/libdl.so (0x70e786b000)
    libc.so => /apex/com.android.runtime/lib64/bionic/libc.so (0x70e4c28000)
ASUS_I006D:/ $
 

The files and directories in the Module are:

FIle/Directory
 content
 Comment
/system/usr/bin/scp
/system/usr/bin/sftp
/system/usr/bin/ssh
/system/usr/bin/ssh-add
/system/usr/bin/ssh-agent
/system/usr/bin/ssh-keygen
/system/usr/bin/ssh-keyscan
/system/usr/bin/sshd		 OpenSSH binaries
/system/bin/scp
/system/bin/sftp
/system/bin/ssh
/system/bin/sshd
/system/bin/ssh-add
/system/bin/ssh-agent
/system/bin/ssh-keygen
/system/bin/ssh-keyscan
 symbolic links to the OpenSSH binaries in
/system/usr/bin and /system/usr/sbin
/system/usr/libexec/sftp-server
/system/usr/libexec/ssh-keysign
/system/usr/libexec/ssh-pkcs11-helper
/system/usr/libexec/ssh-sk-helper
/system/usr/libexec/sshd-auth
/system/usr/libexec/sshd-session

 OpenSSH helper programs
/data/local/tmp/var/
/data/local/tmp/var/empty
/data/local/tmp/var/log
/data/local/tmp/var/mail
/data/local/tmp/var/run
/data/local/tmp/home

 writable data directories for ssh and sshd
 These directories will be created by the customization script if they do not yet exist.

The data in these directories is not changed when the Magisk Module is reinstalled or updated

The directory /data/local/tmp/var/empty is only used if the sshd is started by the user root. The owner of the directory must be the user root.



/data/local/tmp/home/.ssh
 .ssh directory of the user starting the sshd
This directory is used for the files known_hosts, authorized_keys and others.

To use another directory for the binaries ssh, scp, and sftp set the environment variable HOME.

To use another directory for the authorized_keys file, modify the file /etc/ssh/sshd_config.

The customization script for the Magisk Module creates the directory /data/local/tmp/home/.ssh it does not yet exist.



/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key
/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub
/etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key
/etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key.pub
 ssh host keys

 The host keys are created by the customization script of the Magisk Module if they do not yet exist.

The host keys are preserved if the Magisk Module is reinstalled or updated

To change or add new ssh host keys, create the keys in the directory /data/adb/modules/openssh/system/etc/ssh, update the file /system/etc/sshd_config, and reboot the phone
Note that the owner of the host keys must be the user shell.



/etc/ssh/ssh_config
 ssh config file
 This will file is preserved if the Magisk Module is reinstalled or updated

To update the file, edit the file /data/adb/modules/openssh/system/etc/ssh/ssh_config and reboot the phone or remount the file /system/etc/ssh_config
/etc/ssh/sshd_config
 sshd config file
 This will file is preserved if the Magisk Module is reinstalled or updated

To update the file, edit the file /data/adb/modules/openssh/system/etc/ssh/sshd_config and reboot the phone or remount the file /system/etc/sshd_config



/data/adb/modules_update/openssh/service.sh
 start script for the sshd








The module service script /data/adb/modules_update/openssh/service.sh starts the sshd automatically after booting the phone if the file /data/local/tmp/home/start_sshd exists.
The sshd is started by the script with the log file /data/local/tmp/var/log/sshd.log if that file exists.
Additional parameter for the sshd started via service.sh can be defined in the file /data/local/tmp/home/.ssh/sshd_parameter.
The sshd is started as user shell.

The file /data/local/tmp/home/start_sshd is NOT created by the customization script of the Magisk Module.


Access via ssh is only possible with a public ssh key. To do this, the public ssh keys of the users who are allowed to connect must be entered in the file authorized_keys.

The location for the file authorized_keys is defined in the file /etc/ssh/sshd_config:

SUS_I006D:/ $ grep ^AuthorizedKeysFile /etc/ssh/sshd_config
AuthorizedKeysFile    /data/local/tmp/home/.ssh/authorized_keys
ASUS_I006D:/ $


The following environment variables are defined for ssh sessions:

ASUS_I006D:/ # grep SetEnv /etc/ssh/sshd_config
SetEnv HOME=/data/local/tmp PS1="[ssh $(id -un )@$(hostname): ${PWD:-}]  "
ASUS_I006D:/ #


Since version 10.0p2.v1.1.0 of the module with OpenSSH 10.x and version 9.9p2.v1.1.0 of the module with OpenSSH 9.x, the privilege separation user is "nobody" so that the sshd can also be started by the root user.



The sshd ignores the user requested by the ssh client (e.g. via the ssh parameter -l ) -- it always opens a shell for the user that started the sshd.


Since version 10.0p2.v1.5.0 and 10.3p1-v1.1.0 of the Magisk Modules with OpenSSH the binaries ssh, scp, and sftp in the Magisk Modules use the environment variable HOME to find the .ssh directory.
If this environment variable is not set, the default home directory is /data/local/tmp/home. The default home directory is also used if the HOME variable is set to “/”,.

Set the environment variable DEBUG to a non-empty string to print the home directory used, e.g.:

ASUS_I006D:/ # HOME="" DEBUG=0 /system/bin/ssh xtrnaw7@192.168.1.164 id
getpwuid[15602]: HOME= -> using fallback: /data/local/tmp/home
getpwuid[15602]: Username=root
xtrnaw7@192.168.1.164's password:
uid=1000(xtrnaw7) gid=1000(xtrnaw7) groups=1000(xtrnaw7),6(disk),10(wheel),959(docker),967(adbusers),970(vboxusers),1002(tftp),1003(plugdev) context=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
ASUS_I006D:/ #

ASUS_I006D:/ $ DEBUG=0 /system/bin/ssh xtrnaw7@192.168.1.164 id
getpwuid[5348]: HOME=/ -> using fallback: /data/local/tmp/home
getpwuid[5348]: Username=shell
xtrnaw7@192.168.1.164's password:
uid=1000(xtrnaw7) gid=1000(xtrnaw7) groups=1000(xtrnaw7),6(disk),10(wheel),959(docker),967(adbusers),970(vboxusers),1002(tftp),1003(plugdev) context=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
ASUS_I006D:/ $

ASUS_I006D:/ $ HOME=/data/local/tmp/sysroot/home/shell  DEBUG=0 /system/bin/ssh xtrnaw7@192.168.1.164 id
getpwuid[6180]: using HOME=/data/local/tmp/sysroot/home/shell
getpwuid[6180]: Username=shell
xtrnaw7@192.168.1.164's password:
uid=1000(xtrnaw7) gid=1000(xtrnaw7) groups=1000(xtrnaw7),6(disk),10(wheel),959(docker),967(adbusers),970(vboxusers),1002(tftp),1003(plugdev) context=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:unconfined_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023
ASUS_I006D:/ $


Notes

Please note that the sshd configuration is somehow not secure to allow the sshd to be started by the user shell!

The sshd can be started by the user shell or the user root. It's recommended to always start the sshd as user shell to not change the permissions for the data files used by sshd.
The default port used by the sshd is 9022; the port is configured in the file /etc/ssh/sshd_config:

ASUS_I006D:/ # grep ^Port /etc/ssh/sshd_config
Port 9022
ASUS_I006D:/ #


The sshd can also be started by another user, however in this case a sshd_config file with the settings for that user is required.


Details for compiling OpenSSH for Android

The binaries are compiled with the Android NDK r27b using the API version 33; they should therefore work on Android 13 and newer versions.

OpenSSH was compiled with these options:

  Privilege separation chroot path: /data/local/tmp/var/empty
            sshd default user PATH: /system/bin
                    Manpage format: doc
                       PAM support: no
                   OSF SIA support: no

The configure options used are copied from the Termux Build script for OpenSSH:

    https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/blob/master/packages/openssh/build.sh

The configure command used to create the config for compiling OpenSSH for Android is in the file

   ./source/myconfigure_system

in the Magisk Module

All patches for OpenSSH from Termux that are useful for a Magisk Module with OpenSSH are applied to the source code.

The patches for OpenSSH in Termux are available here:

    https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/tree/master/packages/openssh

The patches used are in the directory ./source/patches in the Magisk Module.
The script source/patches/apply_patches.sh in the ZIP file with the Magisk Module can be used to apply the patches.

An additional patch was necessary to get the binaries from OpenSSH working for the user shell:

Source: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76376942/openssh-9-3p-fails-to-build-for-android
(This is the patch misc.c.additional.patch in the directory source/patches in this Magisk Module)


To add support for the environment variable HOME for the binaries ssh, scp, and sftp, add the object file my_getpwuid_system.o as first object file to the link command for that binary. This module defines a modified getpwuid function (without this object module the linker uses the function getpwuid from the standard libraries).
See the script source/compile_ssh_system.sh in the Magisk Module for an example.

The file getpwuid_system.o and the file with the source code for that object file, getpwuid_system.c, are in the directory ./source in the Magisk Module.

The commands to build getpwuid_system.o are:

NDK=/data/develop/android/android-ndk-r27b
${NDK}/toolchains/llvm/prebuilt/linux-x86_64/bin/aarch64-linux-android33-clang  -c my_getpwuid_system.c -o my_getpwuid_system.o

${NDK}/toolchains/llvm/prebuilt/linux-x86_64/bin/llvm-ar rcs libmyuid_system.a my_getpwuid_system.o


---

Trouble Shooting

To execute the customize script of the Magisk Module with "set -x" and write STDOUT and STDERR to the file /data/local/tmp/openssh_customize.log create the file /data/local/tmp/debug before installing the Magisk Module:

touch /data/local/tmp/debug

To execute the service script to start the sshd with "set -x" and write STDERR and STDLOG messages to the file /data/local/tmp/start_sshd.log create the file /data/local/tmp/debug before rebooting the phone.

hostname resolution via DNS is not possible if the sshd was started via the Magisk service.sh script and the current user in the ssh session is NOT the root user. To work around this issue, either restart the sshd in an adb session or execute the commands that need hostname resolution via DNS in the ssh sessions as user root. The script

restart_ssh_daemon

can be used in an adb or ssh session to restart the sshd.


To debug connections problems, start the sshd in debug mode with the parameter -d (and optional another port using the parameter -p portnumber to start it in parallel to the sshd started by the service.sh script ).

Example:

/system/bin/sshd -d -p 8022


Due to the energy saving functions of Android, the wifi connection can be put into sleep mode too often, so that the ssh connection to the phone is very sluggish. To work around this problem, start a ping command in the background to use the WIfi connection continuously, e.g:

ping -i 0.2 192.168.1.1 >/dev/null &

Documentation for the Magisk Module with openssl

The Magisk Module openssl contains the OpenSSL binary for Android on arm64 CPUs:

ASUS_I006D:/ # date
Mon Jun 15 11:18:18 CEST 2026
ASUS_I006D:/ #

ASUS_I006D:/ # openssl --version
OpenSSL 3.5.7 9 Jun 2026 (Library: OpenSSL 3.5.7 9 Jun 2026)
ASUS_I006D:/ #



Also included are the libraries and include files to use OpenSSL in other programs and the documentation.

The OpenSSL binaries are installed in the directory /system/usr/; a symbolic link for the executable openssl is created in the directory /system/bin.

The libraries to use OpenSSL in other programs are installed in the directory /system/usr/lib; the include files are in the directory /system/usr/include/openssl.

The OpenSSL binary can, for example, used to view the certificate used to create the installed OS image using this command:

unzip -p /system/etc/security/otacerts.zip  *pem | openssl x509  -noout -text

Documentation for the Magisk Module with OpenVPN

The Magisk Module with OpenVPN contains the openvpn binary compiled for arm64 CPUs.

ASUS_I006D:/ # date
Mon Jun 15 11:20:20 CEST 2026
ASUS_I006D:/ #

ASUS_I006D:/ # openvpn --version
OpenVPN 2.7.4 aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu [SSL (OpenSSL)] [LZO] [LZ4] [EPOLL] [MH/PKTINFO] [AEAD] [DCO]
library versions: OpenSSL 3.5.7 9 Jun 2026, LZO 2.10
DCO version: N/A
Originally developed by James Yonan
Copyright (C) 2002-2026 OpenVPN Inc <sales@openvpn.net>
Compile time defines: enable_async_push=no enable_comp_stub=no enable_crypto_ofb_cfb=yes enable_dco=auto enable_dco_arg=auto enable_debug=yes enable_dlopen=unknown enable_dlopen_self=unknown enable_dlopen_self_static=unknown enable_dns_updown_by_default=yes enable_fast_install=needless enable_fragment=yes enable_iproute2=no enable_libtool_lock=yes enable_lz4=yes enable_lzo=yes enable_management=yes enable_ntlm=yes enable_pam_dlopen=no enable_pedantic=no enable_pkcs11=no enable_plugin_auth_pam=no enable_plugin_down_root=yes enable_plugins=yes enable_port_share=yes enable_selinux=no enable_shared=yes enable_shared_with_static_runtimes=no enable_small=no enable_static=yes enable_systemd=no enable_werror=no enable_win32_dll=yes enable_wolfssl_options_h=yes with_aix_soname=aix with_crypto_library=openssl with_gnu_ld=yes with_mem_check=no with_openssl_engine=auto with_sysroot=no
ASUS_I006D:/ #
 


The openvpn binary only needs the standard libraries from the Android OS:

ASUS_I006D:/ #  myldd openvpn

# Executing ldd "/system/bin/openvpn"
    linux-vdso.so.1 => [vdso] (0x785d625000)
    libc.so => /apex/com.android.runtime/lib64/bionic/libc.so (0x78584dd000)
    libdl.so => /apex/com.android.runtime/lib64/bionic/libdl.so (0x785862d000)
ASUS_I006D:/ #



The Magisk module also contains the binary dig for resolving IPs via DNS server. Also included is a simple /etc/resolv.conf using public available DNS server:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ cat /etc/resolv.conf 
nameserver 8.8.8.8
nameserver 1.1.1.1

ASUS_I006D:/ $

To use dig with another nameserver use this syntax:

dig www.ibm.com @<ip_of_the_nameserver>

e.g

ASUS_I006D:/ $ dig www.ibm.com @8.8.8.8 +short
outer-global-dual.ibmcom-tls12.edgekey.net.
e7817.dscx.akamaiedge.net.
23.42.94.71
ASUS_I006D:/ $



For testing network connections, the binaries ncat and telnet are also part of this Magisk Module.



The openvpn executable must be executed by the root user.


For testing the VPN connection; I added the OpenVPN config for one of the public VPN server listed on the page

https://www.vpngate.net

in the directory

/system/etc/openvpn/vpngate


The VPN server listed on that page can be used without creating an account. However, please note that the VPN servers listed on that page are intended for development and testing purposes and may not always work!



Use the command

openvpn --config /system/etc/openvpn/vpngate/vpngate.ovpn 

to create a VPN connection using the sample VPN server config.


To check that the VPN connection is working, use for example this command:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ ip route get 8.8.8.8
8.8.8.8 dev tun0 src 10.211.1.169 uid 2000
    cache
ASUS_I006D:/ $


If the routing is via tun0 interface the VPN connection is working.


Note that the OpenVPN config for this VPN server uses the command

ip rule add pref 10 from all lookup main

to route ALL network traffic via the VPN server.


If you're using an Android distribution with integrated firewall like /e/, you must open the IP and port used for the VPN server in the firewall.

For example:

In /e/ the firewall is implemented using iptables.

If the firewall is implemented using iptables, the iptables command to allow a VPN connection to the server 47.154.109.161 using the port 1368 is:

/system/bin/iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 47.154.109.161 --dport 1368 -j ACCEPT
If there is only one rule for a connection, the rule can be deleted using this command:

/system/bin/iptables -D OUTPUT -p tcp -d 47.154.109.161 --dport 1368 -j ACCEPT


To simplify these configuration tasks, the Magisk Module contains a small script for iptable based firewalls:

/system/bin/open_port_in_firewall.sh

This script can be used to add the firewall rule to open the port for using the VPN server.


The usage for the script ist

ASUS_I006D:/ # open_port_in_firewall.sh -h

 /system/bin/open_port_in_firewall.sh v1.0.0 - add or delete firewall rules for the connection to an IP address

 Usage: /system/bin/open_port_in_firewall.sh  [-h|--help] [--in|--out|--both] [--tcp|--udp|--all] [-v|--verbose] [-V] [var=value] [enable|disable|check|status] [vpn_config_file|ip:port]

 "ip:port" is an IP address with a port, e.g:  47.154.109.161:1368
 If the binary "dig" is available via PATH, "ip" can also be a hostname

 Use either the parameter "vpn_config_file" or the parameter "ip:port"

 The default direction is "out"
 The default protocoll is "tcp"
 The default action is "status"
 The default vpn config file is "/system/etc/openvpn/vpngate/vpngate.ovpn"

 Use the parameter "-h -v" to print the detailed usage help

ASUS_I006D:/ #

 

The detailed usage for the script is

open_port_in_firewall.sh -h -v
ASUS_I006D:/ # open_port_in_firewall.sh -h -v
INFO: Processing the parameter ...
INFO: The parameter for the script are
-h -v
INFO: Processing the parameter "-h" ...
INFO: Processing the parameter "-v" ...

 /system/bin/open_port_in_firewall.sh v1.0.0 - add or delete firewall rules for the connection to an IP address

 Usage: /system/bin/open_port_in_firewall.sh  [-h|--help] [--in|--out|--both] [--tcp|--udp|--all] [-v|--verbose] [-V] [var=value] [enable|disable|check|status] [vpn_config_file|ip:port]

 "ip:port" is an IP address with a port, e.g:  47.154.109.161:1368
 If the binary "dig" is available via PATH, "ip" can also be a hostname

 Use either the parameter "vpn_config_file" or the parameter "ip:port"

 The default direction is "out"
 The default protocoll is "tcp"
 The default action is "status"
 The default vpn config file is "/system/etc/openvpn/vpngate/vpngate.ovpn"

 Known parameter:
 
 --in             only process incoming connections
 --out            only process outgoing connections
 --both           process incoming and outgoing connections
 
 --tcp            only process TCP connections
 --udp            only process UDP connections
 --all            process TCP and UDP connections
 
 --verbose -v     print more messages
 -V               print the version number and exit the script
 
 var=value        set the variable "var" to the value "value"
 
 enable or open   open the ip:port in the firewall, "enable_all" is an alias for "enable --both"
 disable or close close the ip:port in the firewall, "disable_all" is an alias for "disable --both"
 check            print the status of the requested firewall rules for "ip:port", "check_all" is an alias for "check --both"
 status           print all firewall rules for "ip:port"
 
 vpn_config_file  VPN config file to retrieve the "ip:port" to use
 ip:port          use this "ip:port" and ignore the vpn config file


ASUS_I006D:/ #



If the script is executed with the parameter open or enable without any other parameter, it adds the firewall rule for outgoing TCP connections to the VPN server configured in the file /system/etc/openvpn/default.ovpn, example:


open_port_in_firewall.sh open
ASUS_I006D:/ $ su - -c open_port_in_firewall.sh open
Using the VPN config file "/system/etc/openvpn/default.ovpn"

*** Processing only outgoing connections

*** Processing only TCP connections

Enabling connections for the IP 47.154.109.161, Port 1368 in the firewall ...
Enabling outgoing TCP connections to the IP 47.154.109.161, Port 1368 in the firewall ....
One or more missing rules added

The firewall rules in place are now:
    0     0 ACCEPT     6    --  *      *       0.0.0.0/0            47.154.109.161       tcp dpt:1368
Checking the result ...
OK; the new firewall rules are now in place

ASUS_I006D:/ $



To delete the firewall rules for the VPN server again use this command:

open_port_in_firewall.sh close
ASUS_I006D:/ $ su - -c open_port_in_firewall.sh close
Using the VPN config file "/system/etc/openvpn/vpngate/vpngate.ovpn"

*** Processing only outgoing connections

*** Processing only TCP connections

Disabling connections for the IP 47.154.109.161, Port 1368 in the firewall ...
Removing these firewall rules for outgoing connections:


7    ACCEPT     6    --  0.0.0.0/0            47.154.109.161       tcp dpt:1368

One or more rules deleted


Checking the result ...
OK; the firewall rules are not active anymore

ASUS_I006D:/ $



To use another VPN config file use this syntax:

open_port_in_firewall.sh <fully_qualified_name_of_the_vpn_config_file>


The script can also be used to add firewall rules to open the port to any IP and port, example:

Add a firewall rule for TCP and UDP connections to and from the server 85.13.142.36 port 443:

open_port_in_firewall.sh --both --all open 85.13.142.36:443
ASUS_I006D:/ $ su - -c open_port_in_firewall.sh --both --all open  85.13.142.36:443
Using the IP and port found in the parameter: 85.13.142.36:443

*** Processing incoming and outgoing connections

*** Processing TCP and UDP connections

Enabling connections for the IP 85.13.142.36, Port 443 in the firewall ...
Enabling outgoing TCP connections to the IP 85.13.142.36, Port 443 in the firewall ....
Enabling outgoing UDP connections to the IP 85.13.142.36, Port 443 in the firewall ....
Enabling incoming connections from the IP 85.13.142.36, Port 443 in the firewall ....
Enabling incoming TCP connections from the IP 85.13.142.36, Port 443 in the firewall ....
Enabling incoming TCP connections from the IP 85.13.142.36, Port 443 in the firewall ....
One or more missing rules added

The firewall rules in place are now:
    0     0 ACCEPT     17   --  *      *       0.0.0.0/0            85.13.142.36         udp dpt:443
    0     0 ACCEPT     17   --  *      *       85.13.142.36         0.0.0.0/0            udp spt:443
    0     0 ACCEPT     6    --  *      *       0.0.0.0/0            85.13.142.36         tcp dpt:443
    0     0 ACCEPT     6    --  *      *       85.13.142.36         0.0.0.0/0            tcp spt:443
Checking the result ...
OK; the new firewall rules are now in place

ASUS_I006D:/ $



Please be aware that the firewall rules created with this script are only temporary and will not survive a reboot of the phone.

To implement persistent firewall rules, create the script /data/adb/modules/openvpn/service.sh. and add the iptables commands to add the firewall rules to that script.


The script open_port_in_firewall.sh is also available here for download: open_port_in_firewall.sh and in this GitHub repository https://github.com/bnsmb/scripts-for-Android.


Since version v2.7-v1.4.0 of the Magisk module, the module also includes an action script for Magisk v28.x or newer to start or stop the OpenVPN daemon.

The action script, which is executed when the action button for the Magisk module is pressed in the Magisk GUI, starts the OpenVPN daemon if it is not running. If the OpenVPN daemon is running, the action script stops the daemon. The script also updates the description for the Magisk module in the Magisk GUI, depending on the status of the OpenVPN daemon.


Examples:



or





The default log file for the OpenVPN daemon if started by the script action.sh is /sdcard/Download/openvpn.log.

The default OpenVPN config file used by the script action.sh is /etc/openvpn/default.ovpn.

In the default config for the Magisk Module, /etc/openvpn/default.ovpn is a symbolic link to /etc/openvpvn/vpngate/vpngate.ovpn.

To use another OpenVPN config file create the file

/sdcard/Documents/openvpn.rc

If the file /sdcard/Documents/openvpn.rc exists, it is sourced in by the script action.sh.

The variables that can be defined in that file are:

# OpenVPN config file
#
OPENVPN_CONFIG_FILE="<fully_qualified_name_of_the_openvpn_config_file"

# log file
#
OPENVPN_LOG_FILE="<fully_qualified_name_of_the_logfile_for_openvpn>"

# additional parameter for OpenVPN
#
OPENVPN_PARAMETER=""

# time to wait for the VPN after starting it in seconds
#
WAIT_TIME=10


To change the default OpenVPN config file used by action.sh, modify the variable OPENVPN_CONFIG_FILE in the file /data/adb/modules/openvpn/action.sh or change the symbolic link for /etc/openvpn/default.ovpn in the Magisk Module


Use the script

/system/bin/start_stop_openvpn

in an adb session to start or stop the OpenVPN manually and update the module description in the Magisk GUI

The usage for the script is:

ASUS_I006D:/ # start_stop_openvpn -h
Usage: /system/bin/start_stop_openvpn [status]
Without parameter the script starts the VPN if it is not running or stops the VPN if it is running
ASUS_I006D:/ #


Please note that starting the VPN via the Action button only works for VPNs that do not require user input for a password or passphrase!

Documentation for the Magisk Module with Perl 5.4x


As of 24.07.2026 the current Magisk Module with Perl contains Perl 5.44.

The Magisk Modules with older versions of Perl are still available for download here:  http://bnsmb.de/files/public/Android/archive/MagiskModules/




The Magisk Module with Perl 5.44 contains the Perl executables compiled for arm64 CPUs.


ASUS_I006D:/ $ perl --version

This is perl 5, version 44, subversion 0 (v5.44.0) built for aarch64-linux-android

Copyright 1987-2026, Larry Wall

Perl may be copied only under the terms of either the Artistic License or the
GNU General Public License, which may be found in the Perl 5 source kit.

Complete documentation for Perl, including FAQ lists, should be found on
this system using "man perl" or "perldoc perl".  If you have access to the
Internet, point your browser at https://www.perl.org/, the Perl Home Page.

ASUS_I006D:/ $


The Perl executables and scripts are installed in the directory /system/usr/bin.


The perl binary is a dynamically linked executable but only for the standard Android OS libraries:

ASUS_I006D:/ # file /system/usr/bin/perl5.44.0
/system/usr/bin/perl5.44.0: ELF shared object, 64-bit LSB arm64, dynamic (/system/bin/linker64), for Android 31, built by NDK r27b (12297006), not stripped
ASUS_I006D:/ #

ASUS_I006D:/ # ldd /system/usr/bin/perl5.44.0
    linux-vdso.so.1 => [vdso] (0x7ee3c6b000)
    libc.so => /apex/com.android.runtime/lib64/bionic/libc.so (0x7ede6a9000)
    libdl.so => /apex/com.android.runtime/lib64/bionic/libdl.so (0x7ede7d5000)
    libm.so => /apex/com.android.runtime/lib64/bionic/libm.so (0x7ede641000)
ASUS_I006D:/ #


 
There is a wrapper script for the Perl executables in /system/bin:

ASUS_I006D:/ # ls -l /system/bin | grep perl_wrapper
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root       14 1970-02-01 23:12 cpan -> ./perl_wrapper
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root       14 1970-02-01 23:12 instmodsh -> ./perl_wrapper
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root       14 1970-02-01 23:12 perl -> ./perl_wrapper
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root       14 1970-02-01 23:12 perl5.44.0 -> ./perl_wrapper
-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root      241 2026-07-21 13:29 perl_wrapper
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root       14 1970-02-01 23:12 perlbug -> ./perl_wrapper
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root       14 1970-02-01 23:12 perldoc -> ./perl_wrapper
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root       14 1970-02-01 23:12 perlivp -> ./perl_wrapper
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root       14 1970-02-01 23:12 perlthanks -> ./perl_wrapper
ASUS_I006D:/ #



The script perl_wrapper sources the file /system/bin/perl_env and executes the original binary:

cat /system/bin/perl_wrapper
ASUS_I006D:/ $ cat /system/bin/perl_wrapper
#!/system/bin/sh

. /system/bin/perl_env

if [ ${0##*/} = perl_wrapper ] ; then
  echo "ERROR: Do not call this script - this is only a wrapper used for the Perl executables"
  exit 254
fi

eval 'exec  /system/usr/bin/${0##*/}  ${1+"$@"}'

ASUS_I006D:/ $
 


/system/bin/perl_env defines some environment variables and sources the file ${HOME}/perl_env if it exists:

cat /system/bin/perl_env
ASUS_I006D:/ $ cat /system/bin/perl_env

# LD_LIBRARY_PATH is only required for some of the object files in this Magisk Module
#
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/system/usr/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}

PERL_HOME_DIR="/data/local/tmp/perl_home"

if [ "${HOME}"x = ""x -o "${HOME}"x = "/"x ] ; then
  export HOME="${PERL_HOME_DIR}"
else
  PERL_HOME_DIR="${HOME}"
fi

PERL5_VERSION_LIB="/system/usr/lib/perl5/system/usr/lib/perl5/5.44.0"


export PERL5LIB="${PERL_HOME_DIR}/lib/perl5:${PERL_HOME_DIR}lib/perl5/aarch64-linux-android:/lib/perl5:${PERL5_VERSION_LIB}"

export PERL_LOCAL_LIB_ROOT="${PERL_HOME_DIR}"

export PERL_MB_OPT="--install_base ${PERL_HOME_DIR}"
export PERL_MM_OPT="INSTALL_BASE=${PERL_HOME_DIR}"

USER_DEFINED_PERL_INIT_FILE="${PERL_HOME_DIR}/perl_env"

if [ -r "${USER_DEFINED_PERL_INIT_FILE}" ] ; then
  echo "${USER_DEFINED_PERL_INIT_FILE} found - now executing it ..."
  echo
  source "${USER_DEFINED_PERL_INIT_FILE}"
fi

ASUS_I006D:/ $



The file ${HOME}/perl_env can be used to define additional environment variables before executing the real perl binaries.




The file ${HOME}/perl_env can therefore be used to define additional variables for the Perl environment


The Perl scripts, such as cpan, do not work with the crippled tool binaries from Android. Therefore, these binaries are also in the Magisk Module in the directory /system/usr/bin:

gpg     gzip     bzip2     less     unzip     wget2     tar     unzip


The customize script in this Magisk Module creates the cpan config file

/data/local/tmp/perl_home/.cpan/CPAN/MyConfig.pm

if it does not yet exist (The config entries in MyConfig.pm use the the binaries in /system/usr/bin).


The customization script also creates the directory /data/local/tmp/perl_home if it does not already exist. This directory is used for the installation of Perl modules.
The directory /data/local/tmp/perl_home is not deleted or modified when the Magisk Module with Perl is updated or deleted.

To list the installed Perl modules execute this command.

perl -MExtUtils::Installed -e '$i=ExtUtils::Installed->new(); for $m (grep {$_ ne "Perl"} sort $i->modules()) { print "$m\n"}'


To test the installed Perl modules for errors execute this command:

perl -MExtUtils::Installed -e '$i=ExtUtils::Installed->new(); for $m (grep {$_ ne "Perl"} sort $i->modules()) { eval "require $m"; print $m, " => ", ($@ ? "ERROR: $@" : "OK"), "\n" }'



The environment variable HOME must contain the name of a directory on a writable filesystem to use cpan.

The wrapper script for the Perl executables in this Magisk Module, /system/bin/perl_wrapper, sets the variable HOME to /data/local/tmp/perl_home if it is empty or contains "/".
(in the default config in adb shells in Android the variable HOME is "/")

To install Perl Modules that require compiling C or C++ source files, install the Magisk Module with the clang19.

The config files in this Magisk Module for installing new Perl Modules are prepared for using the clang Compiler and the Android NDK from the Magisk Module with the clang19.

To install Perl Modules with C source code using the clang compiler from that Magisk Module execute these commands:

# init the clang19 environment (must only be done once in an adb session)
#
source /system/bin/init_clang19_env 

# compile and install the Perl Module
#
cpan install <perl_mdoule_name>


The Perl configuration for compiling new Perl modules with a C or C++ compiler is in the files

/system/usr/lib/perl5/5.44.0/aarch64-linux-android/Config_heavy.pl

/system/usr/lib/perl5/5.44.0/aarch64-linux-android/Config.pm

Edit this file to use a different C compiler when creating new Perl modules.

Note:

To modify these files, edit the files in the Magisk Module in /data/adb/modules/perl544/system/usr/lib/perl5/5.44.0/aarch64-linux-android, as user root and reboot the phone.



How to build the Perl binary


The Perl binaries were build using the clang19 and the Android NDK from this Magisk Module:

http://bnsmb.de/Magisk_Modules.html#Documentation_for_the_Magisk_Module_with_clang19_and_the_NDK_r27b

The Bison/yacc binary used build Perl are from this Magisk Module

http://bnsmb.de/files/public/Android/MagiskModules/bison_flex_1.2.0.zip

The additional include files and libraries required to compile Perl are in the directories ./system/usr/include and ./system/usr/lib in the Magisk Module.

Documentation for the Magisk Module with protoc

Documentation for the Magisk Module with protoc

The Magisk Module with protoc contains the protoc binaries, libraries and data files from the repository

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf

for arm64 CPUs.


ASUS_I006D:/ # protoc --version
libprotoc 32.1
ASUS_I006D:/ #

These binaries and datafiles implement the "Protocol Buffers - Google's data interchange format" (for more infos about Protocol Buffers see here: https://protobuf.dev/)


The binaries are dynamically linked but only for the standard Android libraries, e.g.:

ASUS_I006D:/ # myldd protoc

# Executing ldd "/system/bin/protoc"
    linux-vdso.so.1 => [vdso] (0x7be87b4000)
    liblog.so => /system/lib64/liblog.so (0x7be08ac000)
    libc.so => /apex/com.android.runtime/lib64/bionic/libc.so (0x7be08d0000)
    libm.so => /apex/com.android.runtime/lib64/bionic/libm.so (0x7bdd646000)
    libdl.so => /apex/com.android.runtime/lib64/bionic/libdl.so (0x7be0849000)
    libc++.so => /system/lib64/libc++.so (0x7bdd6b4000)
ASUS_I006D:/ #


Protocol buffers are used in Android for various purposes -- one of them is the file containing infos about an OS image in the ZIP file with the OS image: metadb.pb.

protoc can be used to decode the metadb.pb file from OS image files using this command:

unzip -p <os_image_file> META-INF/com/android/metadata.pb | protoc --decode_raw

Example:

┌shell@localhost:/

For more details regarding the Python Magisk Modules for Android see this entry.


Details for compiling Python3 3.10 for Android
The binaries are compiled with the gcc toolchain from the Android NDK r17c using the API version 21 on a phone running Android 14.


Python3 has been compiled with these configure options (copied from the Termux repository entry for Python3)


export CFLAGS="$CFLAGS -D__ANDROID_API__=21 -O3 "
export CPPFLAGS="$CFLAGS"

export TARGET_ROOT=/data/local/tmp/python3.10

AC_OPTIONS="ac_cv_func_shm_unlink=no  ac_cv_func_shm_open=yesac_cv_posix_semaphores_enabled=yes ac_cv_func_linkat=no ac_cv_func_faccessat=no  ac_cv_file__dev_ptc=no"

eval ${AC_OPTIONS} ./configure  --prefix=${TARGET_ROOT}/usr --with-openssl=/data/local/tmp/develop/sysroot/usr \
   --enable-loadable-sqlite-extensions --enable-shared   --with-builtin-hashlib-hashes=md5,sha1,sha2,sha3,blake2,sha256,sha512 \
   --with-system-expat --without-ensurepip  --with-tzpath=/system/usr/share/zoneinfo --with-system_libmpdec  


Result:


The necessary bits to build these optional modules were not found:
_dbm                  _posixshmem           _tkinter          
nis                   spwd                                    
To find the necessary bits, look in setup.py in detect_modules() for the module's name.


The following modules found by detect_modules() in setup.py, have been
built by the Makefile instead, as configured by the Setup files:
_abc                  pwd                   time              


Failed to build these modules:
grp     


All approbiate patches from the Termux repository for Python

https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/tree/master/packages/python

are applied.

The patches applied are in the directory source/patches in the Magisk Module.

Note:
 
The documentation below is only valid for the version 3.14-v2.0.0 or newer of the Magisk Module.

The documentation for the version 3.14-v1.1.0 of this Magisk Module is here https://xdaforums.com/t/module-python-3-14-for-android.4696862/


Documentation for the Magisk Module with Python 3.14

The Magisk Module python3_3.14 contains Python3 3.14 compiled for Android on an arm64 CPU.

ASUS_I006D:/ $ python --version
Python 3.14.0
ASUS_I006D:/ $

In the module version 3.14-v2.1.0 the binaries were compiled using the source code of the official Python 3.14 release.


Also included in the Magisk Module are the OpenSSL libraries necessary to use SSL in Python scripts (in /system/usr/lib to avoid overwriting OpenSSL libraries from the OS).

Since version 3.14-v2.2.0 the Magisk Module also contains all libraries required by the Python modules in the Magisk Module (in the directory /system/usr/lib).

The Python module to install other modules, pip, is already installed:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ pip --version
pip 25.2 from /system/usr/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pip (python 3.14)
ASUS_I006D:/ $


ASUS_I006D:/ $ pip list
Package Version
------- -------
pip     25.2
ASUS_I006D:/ $ 



The configured directories for site-packages in this Python installation are:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ python3 -m site
sys.path = [
    '/',
    '/system/usr/lib/python314.zip',
    '/system/usr/lib/python3.14',
    '/system/usr/lib/python3.14/lib-dynload',
    '/system/usr/lib/python3.14/site-packages',
    '/data/local/tmp/home/python3.14/site-packages',
    '/data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages',
]
USER_BASE: '/data/local/tmp/home/.local' (doesn't exist)
USER_SITE: '/data/local/tmp/home/.local/lib/python3.14/site-packages' (doesn't exist)
ENABLE_USER_SITE: True
ASUS_I006D:/ $


The directories

/data/local/tmp/home/python3.14/site-packages
/data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages
/data/local/tmp/.local/lib/python/lib/python3.14/site-packages

are writable by the user shell and can be used to add additional site-packages (either manual or via the Python module pip).

Use the command

pip list -v

to list the installed Python modules , e.g:

ASUS_I006D:/ $ pip list -v
Package Version   Location                                  Installer
------- --------- ----------------------------------------- ---------
distro  1.9.0     /data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages pip
pip     25.2      /system/usr/lib/python3.14/site-packages  pip
selinux 0.3.0     /data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages pip
yt-dlp  2025.9.26 /data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages pip
ASUS_I006D:/ $


All Python executables in the directory /system/bin are symbolic links to the wrapper script /system/bin/python_wrapper.


The wrapper script is used to init the environment for the Python executables.


pip can be used to install additional Python modules; the target directory for these modules defined in the wrapper script is

/data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages

To use another target directory for the Python modules export the variable PIP_TARGET before executing pip.

Or use the parameter "--target=<dir>" for pip to set the target directory for the Python modules.

Note that the Python scripts installed with pip are then in the directory /data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages/bin.


The wrapper script defines the environment variable SSL_CERT_DIR with the value /system/etc/security/cacerts if it is not already defined.

The wrapper script defines the environment variable CERTIFICATE_BUNDLE_FILE with the value /data/local/tmp/home/ca-certificates.crt if that file exists and the environment variable is not yet defined.
The file /data/local/tmp/home/ca-certificates.crt is created by the customization script of the module with all SSL certificates found in the directories /system/etc/security/cacerts*.


Use the command

python -c "import ssl; print(ssl.get_default_verify_paths()) " 

to show which certificate paths are being used. E.g.

ASUS_I006D:/ $ python -c "import ssl; print(ssl.get_default_verify_paths()) "
DefaultVerifyPaths(cafile='/data/local/tmp/home/ca-certificates.crt', capath='/system/etc/security/cacerts', openssl_cafile_env='SSL_CERT_FILE', openssl_cafile='/data/local/tmp/develop/sysroot/usr/ssl/cert.pem', openssl_capath_env='SSL_CERT_DIR', openssl_capath='/data/local/tmp/develop/sysroot/usr/ssl/certs')
ASUS_I006D:/ $



The wrapper script defines the environment variable PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX with

/data/local/tmp/home/python/cache

This directory is then used for the compiled Python scripts (the customization script in the module creates this directory if it does not yet exist).


The wrapper script defines the variable TERMINFO with /system/etc/terminfo or /system_ext/etc/terminfo if one of these directories exists and the variable TERMINFO is not already defined


The wrapper scripts sets the environment variable LD_LIBRARY_PATH to

/system/usr/lib


If the directory

/data/local/tmp/home/libs

exists it is also added to the environment variable LD_LIBRARY_PATH. This directory should be used for additional libraries required by the Python scripts.


Set the environment variable DEBUG to any non-empty string before executing python to execute the wrapper script with "set -x", e.g.:

DEBUG=yes python --version          


Example:

DEBUG=yes python --version
ASUS_I006D:/ $  DEBUG=yes python --version
+ CUR_NAME=python
+ CMD_PARAMETER=''
+ export 'HOME=/data/local/tmp/home'
+ '[' x '=' x ']'
+ export 'PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/data/local/tmp/home/python/cache'
+ mkdir -p /data/local/tmp/home/python/cache
+ PYTHON_BASE_DIR=/system
+ PYTHON_BIN_DIR=/system/usr/bin
+ PYTHON_LIB_DIR=/system/usr/lib
+ '[' /system_ext/etc/terminfox '=' x ']'
+ export 'LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/system/usr/lib:'
+ '[' -d /data/local/tmp/home/libs ']'
+ '[' x '=' x ']'
+ export 'SSL_CERT_DIR=/system/etc/security/cacerts'
+ '[' x '=' x ']'
+ '[' -r /data/local/tmp/home/ca-certificates.crt ']'
+ export 'SSL_CERT_FILE=/data/local/tmp/home/ca-certificates.crt'
+ '[' x '=' x ']'
+ export 'PIP_TARGET=/data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages'
+ CUR_BINARY=/system/usr/bin/python
+ '[' ! -x /system/usr/bin/python ']'
+ '[' -r /data/local/tmp/home/python_init.sh ']'
+ eval 'exec  ${CUR_BINARY} ${CMD_PARAMETER} ${1+"$@"}'
+ /system/usr/bin/python --version
Python 3.14.0
ASUS_I006D:/ $






If the file

/data/local/tmp/home/python_init.sh

exists, it will be sourced in by the wrapper script before executing the Python binary.

The file /data/local/tmp/home/python_init.sh can be used to define or overwrite the environment variables for Python ( ... or do anything else)

(see https://docs.python.org/3/using/cmdline.html for a list of supported environment variables; use the variable "$0" in the script to distinguish between the executables)



Installing Python modules with pip

Additional Python modules or scripts can be installed using pip. E.g to install Meson execute the command

pip install meson


Example:

# the installation of newer version of meson seems to be different

ASUS_I006D:/ $ pip install meson==1.7.1
Collecting meson==1.7.1
  Downloading meson-1.7.1-py3-none-any.whl.metadata (1.8 kB)
Downloading meson-1.7.1-py3-none-any.whl (991 kB)
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 991.6/991.6 kB 1.1 MB/s  0:00:00
Installing collected packages: meson
Successfully installed meson-1.7.1
WARNING: Target directory /data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages/mesonbuild already exists. Specify --upgrade to force replacement.
WARNING: Target directory /data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages/share already exists. Specify --upgrade to force replacement.
WARNING: Target directory /data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages/bin already exists. Specify --upgrade to force replacement.
ASUS_I006D:/ $


The default target directory for additional Python Module is

/data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages


So the Meson executable is here:

/data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages/bin/meson


The shebang used in Python executables installed via pip is #/system/usr/bin/python3 (which is correct but not working in this environment) therefore the execution of the executable fails:

ASUS_I006D:/ $  /data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages/bin/meson                                                                                                       
CANNOT LINK EXECUTABLE "/system/usr/bin/python3": library "libpython3.14.so.1.0" not found: needed by main executable
1|ASUS_I006D:/ $


To get around this issue and also ensure that the environment for Python is initialized, either use python to run the executable, e.g.

ASUS_I006D:/ $ python3 /data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages/bin/meson --version
1.7.2
ASUS_I006D:/ $


Or change the shebang in the file to #/system/bin/python3, e.g.

ASUS_I006D:/ $ head -1  /data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages/bin/meson
#!/system/bin/python3
ASUS_I006D:/ $

ASUS_I006D:/ $ /data/local/tmp/home/python/site-packages/bin/meson --version
1.7.2
ASUS_I006D:/ $
